name: ESLint
one_liner: The standard JavaScript linter, with unmatched ecosystem breadth.
what_it_is: A pluggable static analysis tool for JavaScript and TypeScript, where effectively every rule is a plugin, configured through a flat config file in current versions.
why_it_matters: ESLint remains the default because its plugin ecosystem is genuinely unmatched — framework-specific rules, accessibility checks and import hygiene all live there. Its weakness is that same configurability: the config, plugin versions and shared presets are a recurring maintenance cost, which is precisely the opening Biome is attacking.
suitable_for: Projects needing framework-specific or accessibility lint rules
Teams with custom rules encoding their own conventions
Anywhere ecosystem breadth outweighs configuration cost
not_suitable_for: Teams that want linting to be zero-maintenance
Very large codebases where lint runtime is a CI bottleneck
